gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on 2026-11-08 the Redodo 12V 100Ah Group 24 Bluetooth ($259.99) and the Vatrer 12V 100Ah Group 24 Bluetooth with 150A BMS ($259.99) sell for $51.10 less than ChatGPT's 'best overall value' LiTime 12V 100Ah Group 24 Bluetooth ($311.09) with the same 1,280 Wh, Bluetooth, low-temp charge cutoff and 5-year warranty, and that the Redodo 12V 100Ah Self-Heating ($251.99) undercuts ChatGPT's cold-weather pick, the LiTime LiHeat Group 24 ($368.99), by $117.
standout_why: BatteryTrail (cited) has maker-store prices dated 2026-11-06 for Battle Born BB10012 ($799), Renogy Pro ($579.99), LiTime Classic ($335.99, now $302.39), SOK, Dakota, CHINS and Renogy Core Mini ($307.99), plus cost-per-cycle, but it does not list Redodo, Vatrer, Epoch, the LiTime Group 24 Bluetooth or any self-heating LiTime, and gives no $/Wh. ExploringOffGrid (cited) names LiTime 100Ah, Battle Born GC2 and LiTime 230Ah with no prices at all. Neither page prices the two $259.99 Bluetooth/low-temp batteries or the $251.99 self-heating one, so the whole-category $/Wh ladder below is new; the dated-maker-price format itself is not.
decides: Confirms LiTime/Redodo/Vatrer-class batteries as the value tier and Battle Born as a 3x-per-Wh premium, but moves the value pick: for Bluetooth + low-temp cutoff at 1,280 Wh, Redodo G24 BT or Vatrer G24 BT (150A BMS, 1,920 W continuous vs 1,280 W) cost $0.203/Wh versus $0.243/Wh for ChatGPT's LiTime G24 BT; for cold weather, Redodo Self-Heating at $0.197/Wh beats LiTime LiHeat at $0.288/Wh unless the shopper wants LiTime's battery-powered (self-powered) preheat mode, which Redodo and Vatrer lack (both heat only from charger input).
